card.name: Commas and links in drug interaction effects
card.fires_on: Punctuation or small words right after a measured drug effect (INR, AUC, creatinine, levels) in interaction text, where a qualifier such as 'which may', 'usually', or 'especially' is likely to follow.

modes.label: Comma after effect
modes.description: A comma after a stated change in a lab value or drug exposure, before a hedging clause.
modes.example: decreased the mean AUC of sorafenib<<,>> which may decrease the antitumor activity

modes.label: Hedge or list of outcomes
modes.description: A word inside a list of possible outcomes or a qualifier such as 'usually' describing how an interaction effect behaves.

modes.label: Noun ending an effect phrase
modes.description: A noun like levels or tests that completes an effect on a measurement.
modes.example: increase the phenobarbital serum<< levels>>; therefore, phenobarbital blood

card.writes: Promotes words of surprise or qualification like 'presumably', 'unexpectedly', 'surprising', 'myster', so a hedged or unexpected remark may come next.
card.plain: It marks the spot after a reported drug-interaction effect where the text usually adds a qualifier or comment.
